Today when asked by my learned friend, you said that you made a statement to the OTP investigators in 1996, and I should like to ask you if in addition to this statement you gave yet another statement to the OTP in 1998 on the 25th of September, and did you also make a statement to the Public Security Centre in Sarajevo on the 8th of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I won't talk to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think, sir, you will be doing no assistance to yourself if you take that attitude. Mr. Vasic here is appearing for the accused. He has a task to undertake. It may not be a pleasant task so far as you're concerned, but our obligation here is to reach the truth in the matter, and we will only reach the truth if your evidence is fairly and properly tested. Now, if you do take that attitude, it would probably mean that we would not be able to take advantage of the evidence which you have given, whereas as it may very well be true. So I do suggest to you that you reconsider that answer. If you'd like some time to do so, we'd be happy to grant it to you, but if you are going to refuse to answer any questions in cross-examination, that will be the end of any further evidence from you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me think about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you like some time to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, right away. Let him repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I'm very grateful to you. Mr. Vasic, I don't think you need to repeat the introduction, but just refer him to the statement, would you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you make a statement to the OTP investigators on the 25th of September, 1998?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I don't know the date. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you a copy of it there, Mr. Vasic? If you could show it to him, it may be of assistance. I couldn't tell you what day I signed something if I'd even signed it last week. It would be fairer, I think, to show him the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. It is the document that was given us by the OTP. It is ID 188 and ID 188A in B/C/S. Would the usher please help me. Your Honours, if the witness cannot recognise this document, I can also give it to him in English if it will help him to remember if he did indeed give the statement or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is one of the ones given to the local authorities, and it would have been in B/C/S as the original, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a statement to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Well, you can show him also the original which is in English which I assume has a signature on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Yes. I signed. This is my signature. But I just don't remember Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the date there. It's somehow too close, and I don't remember giving any such -- any statements in such a near past, but I can't remember really. Somehow it's just too short a time ago, only two years ago, and I don't remember giving it at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you gave this statement, did you then read and sign every page of that statement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I usually signed separately the pages of the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We got no translation of that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not know if this is your signature, because there is a signature on every page, but we do not know if it is yours.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: This is my signature, and this here is my signature also. This is quite clear. But one signature here is just something I cannot comprehend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us on which page is this unusual signature? Do you believe this not to be your signature?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many pages was the statement that you gave to the OTP investigators long?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On 8 November 1992 did you give a statement to the police in the Public Security Centre in Sarajevo? I will give you a statement shortly so that you can verify whether it is indeed your statement and whether it is your signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a document ID 189 in B/C/S and ID 189A in English.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Yes, this is mine. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When asked by my learned friend today, you stated that you did know Milorad Krnojelac prior to the war.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whether you have observed any anti-Muslim sentiments or attitudes in him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Could you please tell us: While you were staying in KP Dom, do you know how many Muslims were detained there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Well, five or six hundred, something around that, from between five to six hundred. Depends when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you left KP Dom in October of 1992, do you know -- and as you left for Kalinovik, do you know how many Muslim detainees remained at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I think around two or three hundred, something around that figure, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in your statement to the Public Security Centre, did you state that when you left KP Dom, 110 detainees remained?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Perhaps I stated that, but I wasn't sure of it, because I could have given that number arbitrarily. I'm sure that the number that remained was greater than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you're saying that this number was greater by two or three times. Are you sure of what you're saying now?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Yes, I am confident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Today you told us that you were not a member of the SDA but you were a supporter. Did you have a membership card of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When asked by my learned friend, you described the events in Pilipovici immediately after your arrest. Did you, in your statement to the -- at the Public Security Centre in Sarajevo, did you state at the time -- and I will now read this out of the statement. This is the last sentence in the last paragraph. I wouldn't read the whole paragraph, because some names are mentioned, and my question pertains to what is stated in the last sentence: "The same people were taken behind the hangar, and they tried shooting them and fired several hundred bullets at them." Is this what you stated?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: No. I said that they were taken away, but how could I have possibly counted how many bullets they fired? I just know that it was a large number, but I certainly couldn't have known the exact number. Can I ask you something? May I ask a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I am afraid that my role in this proceedings is such that I'm the one who is putting questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may be, however, that the witness only wants to know something which can easily be answered. Perhaps if he asks the Trial Chamber what it is he wants to know, we'll find out whether it's something which you should be telling him, Mr. Vasic. Sir, you may ask us what it is you want to know and we'll see what we can do about answering it for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I want to ask -- when the Defence counsel asked me whether I was a member of the SDA, I was not, but I want to know whether he himself was a member of the SDS or a member of the Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and then came here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the very sort of thing, sir, that we are not interested in. You may be interested in it, but we are not. Mr. Vasic here is here as a counsel, a lawyer who is representing his client to the best of his ability. What his views are are quite irrelevant. It is obvious from his name that he is a Serb, but that doesn't mean that he has any political views, and we are not concerned as to whether he has. And I suggest to you, sir, that you should just put that to one side. If there's something which the members of this Trial Chamber have learnt since being here, the feelings between the different ethnicities remains very strong, and we understand that, but we are trying not to let those feelings interfere with the proceedings here. So please, sir, you answer his questions. Don't worry about what his political views are or may be. You proceed, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I can reply to the witness. I was never a member of any political party. I hope this alleviates the issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is the following: Did you state at the Public Security Centre that these people attempted to shoot?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I did not say that they attempted to shoot; I said that they were shot, which is what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I read to you what was stated in the statement that you supposedly read and signed. Did you read the statement of yours?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I did. I probably did. I know for a certainty that these people were shot. I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Today you told us that people were beaten in an isolation cell which was in the back section of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to show to the witness document 6/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, sir, I would like to point on this drawing to the isolation cells. Can I please ask you to point to where the -- to point to isolation cells where all these beatings took place.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Here, here. One, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness points to the right section of the administrative building from the entrance, from left to the right, he pointed to the third and fourth room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The ones which bear the numbers "1" and "2."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The rooms labelled as Room 1 and 2, and a hall. Thank you, sir. We will not be needing this drawing any more.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: These are the isolation cells. I was here in this building across in pavilion number 1, and my bed was right next to the window, so I would see all this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. My learned colleague asked you whether you were mistreated during interrogation, and I would like to ask you whether you had been mistreated at all while you were staying at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have to undergo any forced labour while you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Today you mentioned that Zelenovic, Zoran Vukovic, conducted the beatings. Were they members of the military police?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you tell the OTP investigators on a court-martial in Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where its headquarters was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Today you mentioned a group of detainees that went plum picking. Can you tell us when?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: September 17th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that together with this group of detainees, two guards who escorted them failed to return as well? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these people taken away by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Guards called out their names, and as to who took them there, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in your statement to the -- in your first statement to the OTP investigators, did you state that the group that went plum picking was ordered by soldiers not to take anything along with them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Today you mentioned that when you were brought to Room 11 where you saw Munib Veiz, Zulfo Veiz, and Mr. Hodzic, you saw them beaten up. Were they beaten up prior to coming to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I don't know. I think not, but I really don't know when they were beaten up. I just know that they were beaten up. Now, whether this happened prior to coming to the KP Dom or after, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. When you left Room 11, did Mr. Munib and Zulfo Veiz remain in that room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you stated that one of the detainees who was a physician helped Dzano Hasan. Could you tell us who it was, please?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Amir Berberkic. He worked in the hospital in Foca, and he was in our room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today when asked by my learned friend, you mentioned a group that was taken out, and at that time you stated that it was mostly people from Josanica and surrounding areas. How do you know this, and could you tell us who was in that group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Hasan Dzano, and people from that area around Josanica. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know these people?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Hasan and Emir and Asim. I knew those three well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the others?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I didn't know them well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then how come you knew that they were from Josanica and surrounding area as well?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the other people in that group, how did you know that they were from Josanica?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Well, when they were taken out, we watched from the window as they were taken out and we saw that all those people were from Josanica and the surrounding area, from villages around Josanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Today you stated that you saw Milorad Krnojelac once in KP Dom and that he was wearing a grey-olive uniform. Was he wearing the old kind of grey-olive uniform?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know that it was a grey-olive uniform. It was in good shape, it looked well. Now whether it was old or new, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in your statement, in your second statement to the OTP investigators, did you state, "I saw him from my cell. He wore a military uniform. It was an old grey-olive uniform"?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Well, it was an old grey-olive uniform that I used to wear myself when I did my compulsory military service, so this is what I meant when I said "old uniform."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were talking about what happened to Mr. Cedic which he had told you himself, and you mentioned a detail concerning the salt. Why didn't you bring this up in any of your previous statements when you were discussing an incident during which Mr. Cedic was injured?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I had forgotten, I really don't know. I probably forgot. I can't keep everything in my mind. A computer would not be able to keep everything in. So I didn't mention this, but that doesn't mean that that's not the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I believe he did mention it in his first statement, the 8th of November, 1992. It's mentioned on the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Your second page may not be the same as Mr. Vasic's second page, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The typed copies are not always the same as the originals.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's true, Your Honour. It's a relatively short statement. It's a two-page statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Tell Mr. Vasic the paragraph, how the paragraph commences.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Well, in relation -- it's more difficult to pick out from the Bosnian statement, but from the English statement, it's on the second page and the fourth paragraph down.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Which statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How does the paragraph commence? That's the only way you can ever pick these things out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: "I wish to point out that Serbian guards maltreated, beat, and subjected people ... and even forced some of them to eat half a kilo of salt, as is the case of Zaim Cedic from Tjentiste," and two or three other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you picked that up, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: As far as we know. Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What's the date of the statement, Mr. Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 8th of November, 1992, and it's in the third paragraph of the B/C/S version on the second page, and on the fourth paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But which statement? Pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The date of the 8th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: To the Bosnian authorities. On the English version it's on the second page, it's the fourth paragraph, and it starts with, "I wish to point out." Your Honour, if I can ask the usher, I can show my copy of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I find it. Thank you. [Interpretation] I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today, when mentioning Mr. Dedovic, Mr. Nurko Nisic, and Mr. Rikalo, you stated that nobody ever saw them afterwards. Can you please tell us: How do you know that nobody ever saw them afterwards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: Well, what kind of a question is this? Everybody knows this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104
utterances.text: The entire population of Foca knows. People from Foca know. People in Sarajevo also know this. They -- everybody knows that nobody ever saw them again. This is -- what kind of a question is this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think what Mr. Vasic is after is: Have people told you that they have never seen any of these men again, or have you been involved in any investigation into where they are? Is that what you're after, Mr. Vasic? You want to know the source from which he can -- he is able to say everybody knows that they have not been seen. Well, ask him, perhaps, again: Who did you hear from that they had not seen those three gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may produce a very long answer and it may be better that we start again with it in the morning. But if I may say to you, sir, the witness, you'll have noticed that Mr. Smith, who is appearing for the Prosecution, is very ready to object to anything which he considers to be unfair. He's asked us to rule on it. So you should leave that to him rather than objecting yourself. You answer the question unless there is an objection taken. We'll resume again tomorrow at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of January, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.59 p.m., to
